arguments.title: W1 rate limiting
arguments.task:
You are implementing work item W1 in the Ledger repo (TypeScript, runs natively on Node 26, no dependencies). Read AGENTS.md first. Rules: run tests with `npm test`; do not add dependencies; import local files with `.ts` extension and use `import type` for types; do NOT change or delete any existing file in test/ (new test files are fine). Work only on your own branch in your worktree; commit your work there; do NOT merge into main. Report the branch name and the commit hash at the end.

Context: src/api.ts has createApp(options: AppOptions) returning { handle(request: Request): Response }. Request = { method, path, headers? (lowercase names) }, Response = { status, headers, body }. A json(status, body, headers) helper exists. src/server.ts calls createApp() and wraps it in node:http. Other agents are concurrently changing api.ts (cursor pagination on GET /invoices; a new POST /invoices route) and server.ts (reading the request body), so keep your api.ts change minimal and self-contained: ideally wrap the existing routing in an inner function and apply rate limiting in the outer handle() so the merge is easy.

Spec (implement exactly):
Handoff code ADM-W1-MB4SJW. The FIRST line of src/rate-limiter.ts must be exactly: // handoff: ADM-W1-MB4SJW
Create src/rate-limiter.ts. It exports createRateLimiter(options: { capacity: number; refillPerSecond: number; now?: () => number }). The result has take(key: string, cost = 1): { allowed: boolean; remaining: number; retryAfterMs: number }.
- It is a token bucket per key. A new key starts with capacity tokens. Tokens refill continuously at refillPerSecond and never go above capacity.
- take() removes cost tokens and returns allowed: true when enough tokens are available. Otherwise it removes nothing and returns allowed: false.
- remaining is the whole number of tokens left after the call (floor).
- retryAfterMs is 0 when allowed. Otherwise it is the milliseconds until cost tokens are available (round up to whole ms is reasonable; be careful with floating-point so it is never too small).
- now defaults to Date.now and returns milliseconds. cost must be an integer from 1 to capacity, otherwise take() throws RangeError.
Wire it into createApp with a new option AppOptions.rateLimit?: { capacity: number; refillPerSecond: number; now?: () => number }. When the option is absent, there is no rate limiting and no new headers (existing tests must still pass).
- The key is the x-api-key request header, or "anonymous" when the header is missing.
- Every request except GET /health takes 1 token (that includes 404s, 405s, and any method/path).
- A limited request returns 429 with the body { "error": "rate_limited" } and the header retry-after, set to the wait in whole seconds, rounded up, minimum 1.
- Every response except GET /health has the header x-ratelimit-remaining (including 429 responses).
- src/server.ts turns rate limiting on with capacity 60 and refillPerSecond 1.

Add thorough tests in a new file test/rate-limiter.test.ts (unit tests of the bucket with an injected clock: refill, cap, partial refill, retryAfterMs, RangeError for cost 0 / non-integer / > capacity, separate keys; and app-level tests: 429 body and retry-after, x-ratelimit-remaining header, /health exempt, anonymous vs x-api-key keys). Make sure `npm test` passes, then commit.
